examples.solution_text:
The factor $5$ cannot be zero. By the null factor law:
$\begin{align*}x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x+4=0\\x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x=-4\end{align*}$

Take out the highest common factor:
$\begin{align*}-6x(x-5)&=0\end{align*}$
The factor $-6$ cannot be zero. By the null factor law:
$\begin{align*}x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-5=0\\x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x=5\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: Solve $6x^{2}=9x$, giving any non-integer solution as a fraction in simplest form.
examples.solution_text:
Rearrange so the right-hand side is zero, then factorise:
$\begin{align*}6x^{2}-9x&=0\\3x(2x-3)&=0\end{align*}$
By the null factor law:
$\begin{align*}x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad 2x-3=0\\x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad 2x=3\\x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x=\frac{3}{2}\end{align*}$

Collect all terms on the left, then factorise:
$\begin{align*}3x^{2}-12x&=0\\3x(x-4)&=0\end{align*}$
By the null factor law:
$\begin{align*}x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-4=0\\x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x=4\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: Alex solves $x^{2}-8x=0$ by dividing both sides by $x$ and writes $x=8$ as the only solution. Explain the mistake and find both solutions.
examples.solution_text:
Dividing by $x$ assumes $x\ne0$, so it loses the solution $x=0$. Factorise instead:
$\begin{align*}x(x-8)&=0\\x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-8=0\\x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x=8\end{align*}$
The factor $x$ gives the zero solution; the other factor gives the second solution.

examples.question_text: The square of a number is $11$ times the number. Write an equation and find every possible value of the number.
examples.solution_text:
Let the number be $x$.
$\begin{align*}x^{2}&=11x\\x^{2}-11x&=0\\x(x-11)&=0\\x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-11=0\\x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x=11\end{align*}$

Expand, collect terms on the left, then factorise:
$\begin{align*}12x-4x^{2}&=2x-x^{2}\\-3x^{2}+10x&=0\\x(10-3x)&=0\end{align*}$
By the null factor law:
$\begin{align*}x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad 10-3x=0\\x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad 10=3x\\x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x=\frac{10}{3}\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: Since 5 is non-zero, 5x(x+4)=0 gives x=0 or x+4=0. Thus x=0 or x=-4.
-6x²+30x=-6x(x-5). The non-zero numerical factor gives no root; x=0 or x-5=0, so x=0 or x=5.
6x²=9x gives 6x²-9x=3x(2x-3)=0. Hence x=0 or 2x=3, giving x=0 or x=3/2.
Subtracting 2x²+14x gives 3x²-12x=3x(x-4)=0. Thus x=0 or x=4.
x²-8x=x(x-8)=0 gives x=0 or x=8. Division by x requires x≠0 and therefore excludes the valid zero solution.
Let the number be x. The statement gives x²=11x, so x(x-11)=0. Every possible value is 0 or 11.
Expanding gives 12x-4x²=2x-x². Collecting gives -3x²+10x=x(10-3x)=0. Hence x=0 or 3x=10, giving x=0 or x=10/3.
